§6Making Muons§f

§aClick to acknowledge: you now understand the muon production chain.§f

This is a checkbox quest. Muons are second-generation leptons produced when pions decay. Pions come from firing proton beams at graphite, beryllium, or tungsten targets in a Target Chamber.

The decay chain goes: proton beam hits target, produces pions, pions decay into muons. Muons can then catalyze fusion reactions in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber.

Muonium is a bound state of a positive muon and an electron, like hydrogen but with a muon instead of a proton. It is a fluid used in exotic recipes.

§ePS:§f Antimuons are the antimatter counterpart. Both are useful in different recipe chains.
